prompt: The planner asks for notification permission a second time, after the student said no. What does the person see?
hint: The system records the first answer.

choices.text: The same system prompt, asking again
choices.why: Apple's documentation says later requests do not prompt the person.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right: the stored answer comes back with no prompt.

choices.text: A prompt sending them to Settings
choices.why: The system shows no such prompt; the app may offer a button of its own.

choices.text: An error the app must show
choices.why: It is not an error: the result is `false`.

prompt: When does the planner ask for permission?
hint: Apple's own example is a task app.

choices.text: At first launch, before anything else
choices.why: Before the person has seen what the app does, the question has no reason.

choices.text: After a week of use, to avoid annoying anyone
choices.why: Waiting a week ties the question to nothing the person just did.

choices.text: When the student turns on a session's reminder
choices.why: Right: the question then answers what they just asked for.

choices.text: Whenever a reminder is about to be scheduled
choices.why: The prompt is shown once; asking every time does nothing after the first.

prompt: For a weekly summary the student never asked for, which authorization does the section call the honest one?
hint: It shows no prompt, and the person decides after seeing one.

choices.text: `.alert` with `.sound`, asked at launch
choices.why: That interrupts for something the student did not ask for.

choices.text: `.provisional`, delivered quietly to Notification Centre
choices.why: Right: the person keeps or turns them off after seeing one.

choices.text: `.badge` alone, so nothing pops up
choices.why: A badge still needs a prompt, and says nothing about a summary.

choices.text: None: send it as a silent background push
choices.why: A silent push shows the person nothing at all.

prompt: The student moves a session from Friday to Saturday. How does the planner change its reminder?
hint: The request's identifier is the session's.

choices.text: It cancels everything pending and schedules the week again
choices.why: That works and is far more than needed.

choices.text: It re-adds the request under the same identifier
choices.why: Right: Apple's documentation says the earlier request is removed and replaced.

choices.text: It edits the pending request's trigger in place
choices.why: A scheduled request is not edited; it is replaced.

choices.text: Nothing: the trigger reads the session's new date
choices.why: The trigger holds the components it was given.

prompt: A session is marked done before its reminder fires. What does the planner do?
hint: A reminder for something done is worse than none.

choices.text: Removes the pending request with its identifier
choices.why: Right: `removePendingNotificationRequests(withIdentifiers:)`.

choices.text: Leaves it: a reminder cannot be cancelled once scheduled
choices.why: It can, by identifier, until it fires.

choices.text: Changes the body to say the session is done
choices.why: A notification about something already done is noise.

choices.text: Asks the student whether to keep it
choices.why: There is nothing to decide: the reminder has no purpose left.

prompt: Match each piece of a local notification to what it holds.
hint: Content, trigger, request.

pairs.right: The date components that say when
An identifier joining content and trigger
How notifications are grouped on screen

prompt: Why does `reminder(forDay:at:)` return components with no time zone?
hint: Where is the student that evening?

choices.text: `DateComponents` cannot hold a time zone
choices.why: It can; the test checks that this one has none.

choices.text: So the reminder fires in UTC everywhere
choices.why: UTC would put it at the wrong hour for everybody not in UTC.

choices.text: Seven in the evening means seven wherever the phone is
choices.why: Right: the phone's own calendar places the hour.

choices.text: Because notifications are delivered by APNs, which has its own zone
choices.why: A local notification never goes through APNs.

prompt: After 25 October in Lisbon, at what hour (local time) did the reminder repeated every 86,400 seconds arrive, according to the capture?
hint: The right-hand column.

prompt: A student in Lisbon wants a reminder every day at 08:00. Which trigger keeps it at 08:00 after the clocks change?
hint: A day is not always 86,400 seconds.

choices.text: `UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger(timeInterval: 86400, repeats: true)`
choices.why: An interval is a duration, and the capture shows it arriving at 07:00.

choices.text: A calendar trigger matching hour 8, minute 0, repeating
choices.why: Right: components ask for the hour and get it on both sides of the change.

choices.text: Either, since iOS adjusts both for daylight saving
choices.why: Nothing in the documentation says an interval is adjusted.

choices.text: A location trigger at her home
choices.why: That fires on arriving or leaving, not at a time.

prompt: What does a repeating `UNTimeIntervalNotificationTrigger` require of its interval?
hint: Its documentation gives a minimum.

choices.text: A whole number of hours
choices.why: Any duration works, above the minimum.

choices.text: At least 60 seconds
choices.why: Right, and nothing about clocks: it is a duration.

choices.text: At most one day
choices.why: There is no maximum in the documentation.

choices.text: A matching calendar trigger
choices.why: The two triggers are separate classes.

prompt: `lisbon.___(after:matching:matchingPolicy:)` is the calendar method the program uses to find the next 08:00.
hint: It finds the next date matching some components.

prompt: The planner is open and a reminder arrives. The delegate does not implement `willPresent`. What happens?
hint: Apple's documentation states the default.

choices.text: It shows as a banner, as it would with the app closed
choices.why: That is what happens with no delegate at all, not with one missing the method.

choices.text: It is not shown
choices.why: Right: the system acts as if the answer were none.

choices.text: The app crashes for lack of the method
choices.why: The method is optional; nothing crashes.

choices.text: It waits until the app goes to the background
choices.why: Nothing in the documentation says it is held.

prompt: Why does the planner's delegate set itself on the notification centre in `didFinishLaunchingWithOptions`?
hint: Think of a tap that opened the app.

choices.text: Because SwiftUI views cannot import UserNotifications
choices.why: They can; the reason is timing.

choices.text: To ask for permission at launch
choices.why: Setting a delegate asks nothing; permission comes later.

choices.text: Set later, it misses what arrived first
choices.why: Right: Apple's documentation says it must be set before the app finishes launching.

choices.text: A delegate set later is ignored for good
choices.why: It works later; it may miss what arrived before.

prompt: How does the delegate know which session a tapped reminder is about?
hint: Section 03 chose the identifier.

choices.text: It looks for the reminder's title among the courses
choices.why: Joining by a title breaks when a course is renamed.

choices.text: From the notification's delivery date
choices.why: Two sessions can share a day; the date does not identify one.

choices.text: It reads the session's id back out of the request's identifier
choices.why: Right: `reminder-` plus the id, written in one place and read in one other.

choices.text: It asks the student with an alert
choices.why: The tap already said which notification.

prompt: Put the steps of a remote notification in order.
hint: Capability, register, token to server, server to APNs.
items: Push Notifications capability added in Xcode
The delegate receives the device token
The app sends the token to the planner's server
The server sends payload and token to APNs

prompt: Without notification permission, what happens to the planner's remote notifications?
hint: Read the documentation for `registerForRemoteNotifications()`.

choices.text: Registration fails and no token arrives
choices.why: Registration does not need permission.

choices.text: They arrive silently, with nothing shown
choices.why: Right: permission is for showing, not for receiving.

choices.text: APNs refuses to send them
choices.why: APNs does not know the person's answer.

choices.text: iOS shows them anyway, once
choices.why: Nothing is shown without authorization.

prompt: Why does the app send its device token at every launch, rather than once?
hint: What would the server hold otherwise?

choices.text: A token expires after 24 hours
choices.why: No such expiry is in the documentation.

choices.text: APNs bills per registration
choices.why: Registration has no charge.

choices.text: A stale token reaches nobody
choices.why: Right, and nothing fails where anyone sees it.

choices.text: To keep the server's connection to the phone open
choices.why: The server never connects to the phone; APNs does.

prompt: What is the maximum size of an ordinary remote notification payload, in bytes?
hint: 4 KB.

prompt: Where does the planner's own key, `session-id`, go in the payload?
hint: Apple's keys have a dictionary of their own.

choices.text: Inside `aps`, beside `alert`
choices.why: `aps` is for the keys Apple defines.

choices.text: Inside `alert`, after `body`
choices.why: `alert` holds what the person reads.

choices.text: At the top level, outside `aps`
choices.why: Right: custom keys go beside `aps`.

choices.text: In an HTTP header of the request to APNs
choices.why: Headers carry delivery details, not the app's data.

prompt: A colleague wants the push to carry the session's whole note, so the app needs no fetch. What does the section say?
hint: The capture measured a long body.

choices.text: Send a summary and an id; the app fetches the note
choices.why: Right: a long note took the payload to 4,616 bytes, which APNs refuses.

choices.text: Fine, as long as the note is compressed before it is sent
choices.why: Compression does not change the rule, and the body must be readable text.

choices.text: Fine for VoIP apps, which get 5 KB
choices.why: The planner is not a VoIP app, and 5 KB is also a limit.

choices.text: Split the note across several pushes
choices.why: Several notifications for one session is worse for the person.

prompt: Why does `encoded(_:)` set `.sortedKeys`?
hint: The capture is compared byte for byte.

choices.text: APNs requires keys in alphabetical order
choices.why: JSON key order means nothing to APNs.

choices.text: So the output is the same on every run
choices.why: Right: without it, two runs may order the keys differently.

choices.text: Sorted JSON is smaller
choices.why: The same keys take the same bytes in any order.

choices.text: Decoding fails on unsorted keys
choices.why: A decoder reads keys in any order.

prompt: Which of these ran on the course's Linux machine? Choose all that apply.
hint: The arithmetic and the JSON did; the framework did not.

choices.text: Working out each reminder's date components
choices.why: Yes: the `remind` program and its tests.

choices.text: Scheduling a `UNNotificationRequest`
choices.why: No: User Notifications is not on Linux.

choices.text: Encoding a payload and measuring its bytes
choices.why: Yes: the `push` program.

choices.text: Receiving a device token from APNs
choices.why: No: that needs a device and a paid account.

prompt: How many bytes did the planner's ordinary push payload take, according to the capture?
hint: The line ending `of 4096`.
